chunks: Abu ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from ʿAlī ibn Samāʿah, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Ribāṭ, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) saying:

The twelve Imams from the family of Muḥammad, all of them are muḥaddath, from the offspring of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the offspring of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام). Thus, the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) are the two parents.

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad, the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الِاثْنَا عَشَرَ: the twelve, referring to the twelve Imams
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely designated leader
key_terms.مُحَدَّثٌ: one who is spoken to or addressed by the angels
key_terms.وُلْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the offspring of the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.وُلْدِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: the offspring of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) say about the twelve Imams being muḥaddath and their lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms that the twelve Imams are from the family of Muḥammad and from the progeny connected to both the Messenger of Allah and ʿAlī (عليه السلام). It also describes all of them as muḥaddath and presents the Messenger of Allah and ʿAlī (عليه السلام) as the two parents, emphasizing the unique lineage and rank of the Imams in Shia doctrine.
